```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false 
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1 <- read.csv("Data/processed/h1.csv")

h2 <- read.csv("Data/processed/h2.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1

Reported political views will have an influence on a composite jealousy in relationships variable (jealousy about emotional infidelity, jealousy about sexual infidelity).

### Variables and descriptive statistics

-   **Reported Political Views (`politics`):** A categorical variable with five groups: Far Left, Center Left, Center, Center Right, Far Right
-   **Jealousy (`jealousy`):** Composite jealousy variable comprised of the mean score across jealousy about emotional infidelity and jealousy about sexual infidelity

```{r}

#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1$politics)

# Summarize jealousy separately for each group.
by(h1$politics, h1$jealousy, summary)

```

### Graph

@fig-jealousy shows the distribution of points by political view. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.
 
```{r}

#| label: fig-jealousy
#| fig-cap: "Relationship Jealousy, by Political View." #adds caption under figure
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h1, aes(x = politics, y = jealousy,
                   fill = politics)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5, point.args = list(alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Political View", y = "Jealousy") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```
 
## H2. Reported financial prospects will have an influence on daily free time.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

-   **Financial Prospects (`financialProspects`):** A single item about future financial prospects. Ranged from 1=Very low, 6=Average, 11=Very high
-   **Daily Free Time (`freeTime`):** The amount of daily free time (in minutes) participants reported having

```{r}

#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2[, c("financialProspects", "freeTime")])

```

### Graph

@fig-freeTime shows the relationship between financial prospects and free time. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}

#| label: fig-freeTime
#| fig-cap: "Financial Prospects and Daily Free Time."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(data = h2,
                 aes(x = financialProspects,
                     y = freeTime)) +
  labs(x = "Financial Prospects",
       y = "Daily Free Time (Minutes)",
       title = "Daily Free Time by Individual Financial Prospects") +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = 0, alpha = .10, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2$financialProspects, h2$freeTime, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2) #rounds the correlation to 2 decimal places
```

The correlation was `{r} round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative association. Respondents who reported higher financial prospects tended to report lower daily free time.
